Tafsir of Surat Alam Nashrah (Surah al-Sharh)
It is a Meccan surah.
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
* *
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ That is: Did We not expand your breast for you? That is, We illuminated it, made it spacious, broad and wide. Like His saying: ﴿So whoever Allah wants to guide - He expands his breast to Islam﴾ [al-An'am: 125]. Just as Allah expanded his breast, so He made His law (shar') broad, wide, tolerant and easy, with no hardship (haraj), no burden (isr) and no constriction (diyq) in it.

It has also been said: what is meant by His saying ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ is the expansion of his breast on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), as has preceded in the narration of Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah [[The takhrij of the hadith has preceded at the tafsir of the first surah of al-Isra'.]], and al-Tirmidhi has also cited it here. This, although it occurred, is not contradictory: for among the totality of the expansion of his breast is what was done to his chest on the night of the Isra', and what resulted from it of the expansion of meaning as well. And Allah knows best.

'Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim [[In A: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman".]] Abu Yahya al-Bazzaz [[In M, A: "al-Bazar".]] related to me: Yunus ibn Muhammad related to us: Mu'adh ibn Muhammad ibn Mu'adh ibn Muhammad ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b related to us: my father Muhammad ibn Mu'adh related to me, from Mu'adh, from Muhammad, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that Abu Hurayrah was bold in asking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about things that no one else would ask him about. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what was the first thing you saw of the matter of prophethood?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat up straight and said: "You have asked, O Abu Hurayrah. I was in the desert, a boy of ten years and some months, when suddenly there was a speech above my head, and a man said to a man: 'Is it he?' [He said: Yes.] [[Addition from the Musnad.]] They met me with faces I had never seen [of any creation] [[Addition from the Musnad.]] ever, and spirits I had never found in any creation ever, and garments I had never seen on anyone ever. Then they came toward me walking, until each one of them took hold of my upper arm, and I could not feel the touch of either of them. One of them said to his companion: 'Lay him down.' So they laid me down without force or violence. One of them said to his companion: 'Split open his chest.' So one of them leaned toward my chest and split it, as I saw, without blood or pain. He said to him: 'Take out the ghill and the hasad.' So he took out something like a clot, then threw it away and cast it off. He said to him: 'Put in the ra'fah and the rahmah.' Then there was something like the silver that he had taken out. Then he shook the big toe of my right foot and said: 'Go forth and be whole.' So I returned with it, going forth, tender toward the young and merciful toward the old."* [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/139), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/222): "its narrators are trustworthy, and Ibn Hibban deemed them trustworthy".]]
* *
As for His saying ﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾, meaning: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your past sins and your future ones﴾ [al-Fath: 2], ﴿which weighed down your back﴾. The inqad is the sound. Many of the salaf said concerning His saying ﴿which weighed down your back﴾: that is, its load was heavy upon you.
* *
As for His saying ﴿And We raised high for you your mention﴾, Mujahid said: "I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned with me: I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

Qatadah said: Allah raised his mention in this world and the Hereafter. There is no preacher, no one who gives the tashahhud, and no one who performs prayer, except that he proclaims it: I testify that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus related to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Jibril came to me and said: Indeed my Lord and your Lord says: How have I raised your mention? He said: Allah knows best. He said: When I am mentioned, you are mentioned with Me." Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, with the same wording. Abu Ya'la related it from the route of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/151).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us, Abu 'Umar al-Hawdi related to us, Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I asked my Lord a question, and I wished I had not asked it. I said: Before me there were prophets, among them one whose wind was subjected to him [[In A: "the sea".]] and among them one who revived the dead. He said: O Muhammad, did I not find you an orphan and give you shelter? I said: Yes, O my Lord. He said: Did I not find you astray and guide you? I said: Yes, O my Lord. He said: Did I not find you destitute and enrich you? I said: Yes, O my Lord. He said: Did I not expand [[In A: "Alam Nashrah".]] your breast for you? Did I not raise high your mention? I said: Yes, O my Lord." [[Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (2/526) through Ahmad ibn Salamah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Jarrah, from Hammad ibn Zayd with the same, and said: "its isnad is sound, but they did not record it".]]

Abu Nu'aym said in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah: Abu Ahmad al-Ghitrifi related to us, Musa ibn Sahl al-Jawni related to us, Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Bahram al-Hiti related to us, Nasr ibn Hammad related to us, from 'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from al-Zuhri, from Anas who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When I finished what Allah had commanded me concerning the matter of the heavens and the earth, I said: O Lord, indeed no prophet came before me except that You honoured him: You made Ibrahim a khalil (intimate friend) and Musa a kalim (one who spoke with Allah), You subjected the mountains to Dawud and the wind and the devils to Sulayman, and You revived the dead for 'Isa. So what did You give me? He said: Did I not give you better than all of that? That I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned with Me, and I made the breasts of your nation gospels reciting the Qur'an openly, which I did not give to any nation, and I gave you a treasure from the treasures of My Throne: There is no power and no might except by Allah, the Most High, the Most Great." [[The author mentioned it in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (6/288) and then said: "This isnad contains strangeness, but I cite as corroboration a route from Abu al-Qasim ibn Mani' al-Baghawi, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Mahrani, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, raised, similar in meaning".]]

Al-Baghawi related from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid that what is meant by that is the adhan (call to prayer), meaning: His mention in it. He cited from the poetry of Hassan ibn Thabit:

Illustrious upon Him is a seal of prophethood, from Allah, of light that shines and bears witness...
And Allah joined the name of the Prophet to His name, when the muezzin says in the five: "I bear witness..."
And He split for Him from His name, to honour him: "Dhu al-'Arsh is Mahmud, and this is Muhammad." [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (8/464).]]

Others said: Allah raised his mention among the first and the last, and exalted him, when He took the covenant from all the prophets that they would believe in him and command their peoples [[In A: "their nation".]] to believe in him. Then He made his mention famous among his nation, so Allah is not mentioned except that he is mentioned with Him.

How excellent is what al-Sarsari said, may Allah have mercy on him:

The adhan in the obligatory prayer is not valid except with his sweet name in the approved mouth...

He also said:

Do you not see that our adhan is not valid, nor our obligatory prayer, unless we repeat it in both? [[Addition from M, A.]]
* *
As for His saying ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease. Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾, Allah the Exalted informs that with hardship ease is found, then He emphasized this report.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us, Mahmud ibn Ghaylan related to us, Humayd ibn Hammad ibn Khuwar Abu al-Jahm related to us, 'A'idh ibn Shurayh related to us, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Prophet ﷺ was sitting, and before him was a stone, and he said: "If hardship came and entered this stone, ease would come until it enters upon it and brings it out." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease. Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. [[In A, H: "in" which is an error; the correct is what we have placed.]] [[Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (2/255) through Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, and said: "this is a strange hadith, except that the two Shaykhs did not take as evidence 'A'idh ibn Shurayh." Al-Dhahabi said: "Humayd ibn Hammad narrated alone from 'A'idh, and Humayd is munkar al-hadith, as is 'A'idh."]]

Al-Bazzar related it in his Musnad from Muhammad ibn Ma'mar, from Humayd ibn Hammad, with it, and its wording: "If hardship came until it enters this stone, ease would come until it brings it out," then he said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease. Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. Then al-Bazzar said: We do not know that anyone related it from Anas except 'A'idh ibn Shurayh. [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2288) "Kashf al-Astar", and al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. (3416) through Muhammad ibn Ma'mar.]]

I say: Abu Hatim al-Razi has said concerning him: "In his hadith there is weakness, but Shu'bah related it from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from a man, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, as a mawquf report."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, Abu Qatan [[In A: "Mutar".]] related to us, al-Mubarak ibn Fadalah related to us, from al-Hasan who said: They used to say: One hardship will not overcome two eases.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, Ibn [[In A: "Abu".]] Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan who said: The Prophet ﷺ went out one day joyful and happy, laughing, and he was saying: "No hardship will overcome two eases, no hardship will overcome two eases, for indeed with hardship there is ease, indeed with hardship there is ease." [[In M, A, H: "in" which is an error. From Ibn Jarir (30/151).]]

Likewise it was related from the hadith of 'Awf al-A'rabi and Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, as a mursal report. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/151). 'Abd al-Razzaq related it in his Tafsir (2/309) from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, as mursal; it also came as a mawquf report on Ibn Mas'ud, related by 'Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir (2/309) through Maymun from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i from him; and it came as a marfu' report from Jabir, related by Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, and al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "its isnad is weak".]]

Sa'id said, from Qatadah: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave his companions good news with this verse, saying: "No hardship will overcome two eases."

The meaning of this is: that the word "hardship" (al-'usr) is definite in both places, so it is one; and "ease" (al-yusr) is indefinite, so it is multiplied. For this reason he said: "No hardship will overcome two eases," meaning His saying: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease. Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. So the first hardship is the same as the second, and the ease is multiplied.

Al-Hasan ibn Sufyan said: Yazid ibn Salih related to us, Kharijah related to us, from 'Abbad ibn Kathir, from Abu al-Zinad, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Help has been sent down from the sky in proportion to the burden, and patience has been sent down in proportion to the affliction." [[Related by al-Bazzar in his Musnad no. (1506) "Kashf al-Astar" and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (4/115) through 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Darawardi, from Tariq and 'Abbad ibn Kathir, from Abu al-Zinad with it. al-Bazzar said: "We do not know it from Abu Hurayrah except by this isnad." Ibn 'Adi said: "Tariq ibn 'Ammar is known for this hadith." The hadith is defective. See: al-'Ilal of Ibn Abi Hatim (2/126, 133) and al-Kamil of Ibn 'Adi (6/238, 402; 2/37; 4/115).]]

It is related from al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said:

Patience, beautiful patience, how near relief is! Whoever is mindful of Allah in matters is saved.
Whoever is truthful to Allah, no harm reaches him, and whoever hopes in Him will be where he hopes.

Ibn Durayd said: Abu Hatim al-Sijistani recited to me:

When hearts are wrapped in despair, and the breast, which was wide, is constricted by what it bears...
And hardships have trampled and settled, and calamities have taken their places...
And no face appears for the removal of harm, nor does the clever man benefit by his stratagem...
There came to you, after your despair, a relief bestowed by the Gentle, the Responder...
And every calamity, when it reaches its end, is joined to a near relief...

Another said:

How often a calamity has constricted a young man's chest, while with Allah is its way out...
It was complete, and when its links became firm, it was relieved, though he thought it would never be relieved...
* *

And His saying: ﴿So when you are free, then strive hard﴾. That is, when you are free from the affairs and occupations of this world and have cut off its ties, then strive in worship, rising to it energetic and with a free mind, and devote your intention and desire sincerely to your Lord. Of this kind is the Prophet's ﷺ saying in the hadith agreed upon as authentic: "There is no prayer in the presence of food, nor while one is being pressed by the two impurities (urine and feces)."[[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (560), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] And the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "When the prayer is called and the evening meal is served, begin with the meal."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (5465), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]]

Mujahid said regarding this verse: "When you are free from the affairs of this world and have stood up for the prayer, then strive for your Lord." In another report from him: "When you stand up for the prayer, then strive in your need." And from Ibn Mas'ud: "When you are free from the obligatory duties, then strive in the night prayer." Similar was reported from Ibn 'Iyad. And in a report from Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿So strive, and to your Lord turn with desire﴾, meaning after your completion of the prayer while you are sitting.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿So when you are free, then strive hard﴾, meaning: in supplication.

Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Dahhak said: ﴿When you are free﴾, that is, from jihad; ﴿then strive hard﴾, that is, in worship; ﴿and to your Lord turn with desire﴾. Al-Thawri said: Make your intention and your desire directed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

End of the commentary on Surah "Alam Nashrah." And all praise is due to Allah.

Ibn Durayd said: Abu Hatim al-Sijistani recited to me:

When hearts are wrapped in despair, and the breast, which was wide, is constricted by what it bears...
And hardships have trampled and settled, and calamities have taken their places...
And no face appears for the removal of harm, nor does the clever man benefit by his stratagem...
There came to you, after your despair, a relief bestowed by the Gentle, the Responder...
And every calamity, when it reaches its end, is joined to a near relief...

Another said:

How often a calamity has constricted a young man's chest, while with Allah is its way out...
It was complete, and when its links became firm, it was relieved, though he thought it would never be relieved...
* *

And His saying: ﴿So when you are free, then strive hard﴾. That is, when you are free from the affairs and occupations of this world and have cut off its ties, then strive in worship, rising to it energetic and with a free mind, and devote your intention and desire sincerely to your Lord. Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 94, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Tafsir of Surat Alam Nashrah (Surah al-Sharh)
It is a Meccan surah.
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
* *
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ That is: Did We not expand your breast for you? That is, We illuminated it, made it spacious, broad and wide. Like His saying: ﴿So whoever Allah wants to guide - He expands his breast to Islam﴾ [al-An'am: 125]. Just as Allah expanded his breast, so He made His law (shar') broad, wide, tolerant and easy, with no hardship (haraj), no burden (isr) and no constriction (diyq) in it.

It has also been said: what is meant by His saying ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ is the expansion of his breast on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), as has preceded in the narration of Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah [[The takhrij of the hadith has preceded at the tafsir of the first surah of al-Isra'.]], and al-Tirmidhi has also cited it here. This, although it occurred, is not contradictory: for among the totality of the expansion of his breast is what was done to his chest on the night of the Isra', and what resulted from it of the expansion of meaning as well. And Allah knows best.

'Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim [[In A: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman".]] Abu Yahya al-Bazzaz [[In M, A: "al-Bazar".]] related to me: Yunus ibn Muhammad related to us: Mu'adh ibn Muhammad ibn Mu'adh ibn Muhammad ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b related to us: my father Muhammad ibn Mu'adh related to me, from Mu'adh, from Muhammad, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that Abu Hurayrah was bold in asking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about things that no one else would ask him about. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what was the first thing you saw of the matter of prophethood?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat up straight and said: "You have asked, O Abu Hurayrah. I was in the desert, a boy of ten years and some months, when suddenly there was a speech above my head, and a man said to a man: 'Is it he?' [He said: Yes.] [[Addition from the Musnad.]] They met me with faces I had never seen [of any creation] [[Addition from the Musnad.]] ever, and spirits I had never found in any creation ever, and garments I had never seen on anyone ever. Then they came toward me walking, until each one of them took hold of my upper arm, and I could not feel the touch of either of them. One of them said to his companion: 'Lay him down.' So they laid me down without force or violence. One of them said to his companion: 'Split open his chest.' So one of them leaned toward my chest and split it, as I saw, without blood or pain. He said to him: 'Take out the ghill and the hasad.' So he took out something like a clot, then threw it away and cast it off. He said to him: 'Put in the ra'fah and the rahmah.' Then there was something like the silver that he had taken out. Then he shook the big toe of my right foot and said: 'Go forth and be whole.' So I returned with it, going forth, tender toward the young and merciful toward the old."* [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/139), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/222): "its narrators are trustworthy, and Ibn Hibban deemed them trustworthy".]]
* *
As for His saying ﴿And We removed from you your burden﴾, meaning: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your past sins and your future ones﴾ [al-Fath: 2], ﴿which weighed down your back﴾. The inqad is the sound. Many of the salaf said concerning His saying ﴿which weighed down your back﴾: that is, its load was heavy upon you.
* *
As for His saying ﴿And We raised high for you your mention﴾, Mujahid said: "I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned with me: I testify that there is no god but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

Qatadah said: Allah raised his mention in this world and the Hereafter. There is no preacher, no one who gives the tashahhud, and no one who performs prayer, except that he proclaims it: I testify that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus related to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Jibril came to me and said: Indeed my Lord and your Lord says: How have I raised your mention? He said: Allah knows best. He said: When I am mentioned, you are mentioned with Me." Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, with the same wording. Abu Ya'la related it from the route of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/151).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us, Abu 'Umar al-Hawdi related to us, Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I asked my Lord a question, and I wished I had not asked it. I said: Before me there were prophets, among them one whose wind was subjected to him [[In A: "the sea".]] and among them one who revived the dead. He said: O Muhammad, did I not find you an orphan and give you shelter? I said: Yes, O my Lord. He said: Did I not find you astray and guide you? I said: Yes, O my Lord. He said: Did I not find you destitute and enrich you? I said: Yes, O my Lord. He said: Did I not expand [[In A: "Alam Nashrah".]] your breast for you? Did I not raise high your mention? I said: Yes, O my Lord." [[Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (2/526) through Ahmad ibn Salamah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Jarrah, from Hammad ibn Zayd with the same, and said: "its isnad is sound, but they did not record it".]]

Abu Nu'aym said in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah: Abu Ahmad al-Ghitrifi related to us, Musa ibn Sahl al-Jawni related to us, Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Bahram al-Hiti related to us, Nasr ibn Hammad related to us, from 'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from al-Zuhri, from Anas who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When I finished what Allah had commanded me concerning the matter of the heavens and the earth, I said: O Lord, indeed no prophet came before me except that You honoured him: You made Ibrahim a khalil (intimate friend) and Musa a kalim (one who spoke with Allah), You subjected the mountains to Dawud and the wind and the devils to Sulayman, and You revived the dead for 'Isa. So what did You give me? He said: Did I not give you better than all of that? That I am not mentioned except that you are mentioned with Me, and I made the breasts of your nation gospels reciting the Qur'an openly, which I did not give to any nation, and I gave you a treasure from the treasures of My Throne: There is no power and no might except by Allah, the Most High, the Most Great." [[The author mentioned it in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (6/288) and then said: "This isnad contains strangeness, but I cite as corroboration a route from Abu al-Qasim ibn Mani' al-Baghawi, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Mahrani, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, raised, similar in meaning".]]

Illustrious upon Him is a seal of prophethood, from Allah, of light that shines and bears witness...
And Allah joined the name of the Prophet to His name, when the muezzin says in the five: "I bear witness..."
And He split for Him from His name, to honour him: "Dhu al-'Arsh is Mahmud, and this is Muhammad." [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (8/464).]]

Others said: Allah raised his mention among the first and the last, and exalted him, when He took the covenant from all the prophets that they would believe in him and command their peoples [[In A: "their nation".]] to believe in him. Then He made his mention famous among his nation, so Allah is not mentioned except that he is mentioned with Him.

How excellent is what al-Sarsari said, may Allah have mercy on him:

The adhan in the obligatory prayer is not valid except with his sweet name in the approved mouth...

He also said:

Do you not see that our adhan is not valid, nor our obligatory prayer, unless we repeat it in both? [[Addition from M, A.]]
* *
As for His saying ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease. Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾, Allah the Exalted informs that with hardship ease is found, then He emphasized this report.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah related to us, Mahmud ibn Ghaylan related to us, Humayd ibn Hammad ibn Khuwar Abu al-Jahm related to us, 'A'idh ibn Shurayh related to us, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Prophet ﷺ was sitting, and before him was a stone, and he said: "If hardship came and entered this stone, ease would come until it enters upon it and brings it out." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease. Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. [[In A, H: "in" which is an error; the correct is what we have placed.]] [[Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (2/255) through Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, and said: "this is a strange hadith, except that the two Shaykhs did not take as evidence 'A'idh ibn Shurayh." Al-Dhahabi said: "Humayd ibn Hammad narrated alone from 'A'idh, and Humayd is munkar al-hadith, as is 'A'idh."]]

Al-Bazzar related it in his Musnad from Muhammad ibn Ma'mar, from Humayd ibn Hammad, with it, and its wording: "If hardship came until it enters this stone, ease would come until it brings it out," then he said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease. Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. Then al-Bazzar said: We do not know that anyone related it from Anas except 'A'idh ibn Shurayh. [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2288) "Kashf al-Astar", and al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. (3416) through Muhammad ibn Ma'mar.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, Abu Qatan [[In A: "Mutar".]] related to us, al-Mubarak ibn Fadalah related to us, from al-Hasan who said: They used to say: One hardship will not overcome two eases.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, Ibn [[In A: "Abu".]] Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan who said: The Prophet ﷺ went out one day joyful and happy, laughing, and he was saying: "No hardship will overcome two eases, no hardship will overcome two eases, for indeed with hardship there is ease, indeed with hardship there is ease." [[In M, A, H: "in" which is an error. From Ibn Jarir (30/151).]]

Likewise it was related from the hadith of 'Awf al-A'rabi and Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, as a mursal report. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/151). 'Abd al-Razzaq related it in his Tafsir (2/309) from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, as mursal; it also came as a mawquf report on Ibn Mas'ud, related by 'Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir (2/309) through Maymun from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i from him; and it came as a marfu' report from Jabir, related by Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, and al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "its isnad is weak".]]

Sa'id said, from Qatadah: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave his companions good news with this verse, saying: "No hardship will overcome two eases."

The meaning of this is: that the word "hardship" (al-'usr) is definite in both places, so it is one; and "ease" (al-yusr) is indefinite, so it is multiplied. For this reason he said: "No hardship will overcome two eases," meaning His saying: ﴿So indeed, with hardship there is ease. Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾. So the first hardship is the same as the second, and the ease is multiplied.

Al-Hasan ibn Sufyan said: Yazid ibn Salih related to us, Kharijah related to us, from 'Abbad ibn Kathir, from Abu al-Zinad, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Help has been sent down from the sky in proportion to the burden, and patience has been sent down in proportion to the affliction." [[Related by al-Bazzar in his Musnad no. (1506) "Kashf al-Astar" and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (4/115) through 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Darawardi, from Tariq and 'Abbad ibn Kathir, from Abu al-Zinad with it. al-Bazzar said: "We do not know it from Abu Hurayrah except by this isnad." Ibn 'Adi said: "Tariq ibn 'Ammar is known for this hadith." The hadith is defective. See: al-'Ilal of Ibn Abi Hatim (2/126, 133) and al-Kamil of Ibn 'Adi (6/238, 402; 2/37; 4/115).]]

It is related from al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said:

Patience, beautiful patience, how near relief is! Whoever is mindful of Allah in matters is saved.
Whoever is truthful to Allah, no harm reaches him, and whoever hopes in Him will be where he hopes.

When hearts are wrapped in despair, and the breast, which was wide, is constricted by what it bears...

* *

And His saying: ﴿So when you are free, then strive hard﴾. That is, when you are free from the affairs and occupations of this world and have cut off its ties, then strive in worship, rising to it energetic and with a free mind, and devote your intention and desire sincerely to your Lord. (560), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] And the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "When the prayer is called and the evening meal is served, begin with the meal."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (5465), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]]

Mujahid said regarding this verse: "When you are free from the affairs of this world and have stood up for the prayer, then strive for your Lord." In another report from him: "When you stand up for the prayer, then strive in your need." And from Ibn Mas'ud: "When you are free from the obligatory duties, then strive in the night prayer." Similar was reported from Ibn 'Iyad. And in a report from Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿So strive, and to your Lord turn with desire﴾, meaning after your completion of the prayer while you are sitting.

End of the commentary on Surah "Alam Nashrah." And all praise is due to Allah.
